fig-182.layout: Two columns and three rows; left column a,b,c; right column d,e,f after transliterating the six source Cyrillic subfigure letters in reading-by-column order.

panels.observed: A at left, a convex lens in the middle, two bounding directed rays meeting on the vertical film line at right.
B nearer the lens than A; the bounding outgoing rays are still separated on the film line. No downstream exact-focus point is drawn.
C farther from the lens than A; outgoing bounding rays cross before the film line and are separated again at that line.
Same A distance and lens/film arrangement as a. Four incoming boundary paths; outer paths end at the aperture bars, inner paths continue and meet on the film line.
Same nearer B case as b. Four incoming boundary paths, outer blocked paths and a narrower transmitted bundle; nonzero film-plane separation is visibly smaller than in b.
Same farther C case as c. Outer blocked paths; narrower transmitted paths cross before film and remain separated on it by less than in c.

sharedStructure: Each lens is centrally thick, with an upright outline, end caps and repeated short diagonal interior marks.
Lens-to-film arrangement is unchanged in the repeated cases, allowing a fixed-film comparison in local panel coordinates.
All ray arrowheads point from the left object toward the right film.
Right-column aperture bars are immediately to the RIGHT of the lens in these actual source pixels, with an open central gap.
Each right-column source point repeats the corresponding left-column distance ordering.
The film is shown edge-on as a vertical line. B' and C' label film-plane defocus locations, not exact conjugate image points.
notInPixels: No numerical focal length, object distance, image distance or aperture diameter.

fig-182.sourceTextTension: The supplied current bilingual prose says the aperture is before the objective. The inspected source places its bars to the right. Keep the source-side position; explicitly declare the image-side-stop thin-lens construction and request independent FIG resolution rather than moving the bars silently.

groups.observed: Left source S is a small radiating star-like light mark inside a large rectangular housing. Short radiating strokes and a right-going illumination fan are visible.
K labels a pair of upright centrally thick lens elements at the housing's right wall. The two facing curved profiles and their short interior diagonal marks remain distinguishable.
D is a narrow upright framed slide just to the right of K, with a diagonal leader from its label.
O labels the smaller lens farther right. It sits in a stepped/rectangular tube extending from the slide area, ending in an upright exit rim.
An unlabeled tall vertical screen stands at far right, beyond the objective.

Directed illumination paths run S to K to D. Multiple paths run from the slide through O, crossing in the objective region, then spreading to the screen; the outer upper/lower paths end well above/below the narrow slide extent.

notInPixels: No focal points, focal lengths, object/image distance numbers, calibrated scale, wavelength, or lens equation.
No separately labeled image endpoints or quantitative magnification.
No claim that condenser K forms the slide image on the screen.
